solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tempting trick putting the Tories, say, back on edge

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: to edge a blade is to hone it, sharpen it

indicators.note: back means the word for the Tories' grouping is read in reverse

parts.note: the Tories are an example of a political party

explanation.surface: A political smear: some ruse that puts the Conservatives back on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge' looks like a noun, a rim, but works as the verb to sharpen; 'back' and 'on' are the reversal and placing signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A seduction set up to compromise someone is a classic tempting trick used by spies and blackmailers.

clue.text: Wash outside of small mugs

indicators.note: outside of tells us the phrase for wash wraps around the letter for small

parts.note: an excuse that will not wash will not hold up: convince or stand scrutiny
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Instructions for the washing-up: clean the outsides of the little cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugs' looks like crockery but is the verb, robs.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug someone is to rob them by force, the same as a street robbery at gunpoint or knifepoint.

clue.text: Cop wanting moratorium lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the word for moratorium is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a moratorium is a ban, a temporary prohibition

explanation.surface: A police officer who wants a suspension of activity to be ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' looks like a noun, a police officer, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop someone, in slang, is to catch or arrest them, a synonym for seizing.

clue.text: Periodicals having mainly long pieces of fiction

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word for long is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn
lies are untruths, invented stories

explanation.surface: Magazines that are mostly full of long stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Publications issued once a year are annuals, one kind of periodical.

clue.text: Verse that's touching about husband upset brother!

indicators.note: about tells us the word for touching goes round the other pieces

parts.note: re, as in a business letter, means concerning or touching on

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the exclamation is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: 'brother!' and 'my!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Poetry that is moving, about a husband who has upset his brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brother!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'; 'upset' flips it in this down clue, and 'about' wraps the touching word round everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is poetry, and a short poem with chiming line endings is a rhyme, as in a nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Shark left tailless by black bird of prey

indicators.note: tailless means the word for left loses its last letter

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A shark is left without its tail by a black raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large mackerel shark of the North Atlantic, a species name.

clue.text: After 11 brewed a sweet drink

indicators.note: brewed means those letters are stirred up and remade

parts.note: the answer to clue 11 across, a rope fibre

explanation.surface: Once eleven o'clock comes, a sweet drink is made.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is not a time but a cross-reference to the answer at 11 across, whose letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Indian yoghurt drink, often served sweetened, so a sweet drink is a fair description.

clue.text: Employment rating in line with a number first rejected

indicators.note: in tells us the rating goes inside the other letters
first rejected means the opening letter of the number is thrown out

parts.note: four is a number
AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: A job grading lines up with a figure that was turned down first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' is a crossword staple for an ordinary sailor; 'first rejected' drops the number's opening letter and 'in' tucks the sailor inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour means work, the toil one is employed to do.

clue.text: Hop down from old-fashioned country steps?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece below another is down from it, so the dance follows

parts.note: square is slang for staid, out of date
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Jump down off some antiquated rural stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country steps' suggests stairs in the country, but means steps of a country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a folk dance of four couples, so its moves are literally steps danced in the country.

clue.text: One name unknown in animals I order into lists

definitions.note: a self-description: the speaker is a person who does this

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in tells us the unknown is placed within the animals

parts.note: deer are animals
X is the mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone sorting animals into lists, with one name missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who compiles an index sorts terms into ordered lists for a book.

clue.text: Record collection, large one, with tracks by British artist

indicators.note: by means set beside, here after the letters before it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist
RY is an abbreviation for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: A large music collection with tracks by a British artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record collection' suggests vinyl albums, but means a store of records such as books.
explanation.definitionFit: A store of books and documents, records in the broad sense, is held in a library.

clue.text: Very likely after queen's returned glance?

indicators.note: after places the word for very likely later than the queen
returned means the queen's letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
something bound to happen is very likely

explanation.surface: A glance which is very likely after the Queen has come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A glancing blow bounces off at an angle, so glance can mean ricochet.

clue.text: Rope maker is getting in a lot of tar

indicators.note: getting in tells us the clue's is goes inside
a lot of means most of the word for sailor is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tar, like an old salt, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A rope manufacturer is taking delivery of a quantity of tar for waterproofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like pitch for ropes but is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plant fibre spun into twine and cordage, so it is a material that makes rope.

clue.text: Catch extremely large second fish

parts.note: a drawer that catches sticks, jams

indicators.note: extremely means take the outermost letters of large

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: Land a very big second fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small spiny freshwater fish familiar from ponds and streams.

clue.text: Will I have to deal with not being a man?

definitions.text: Will I have to deal with not being a man?

parts.words: Will I have to deal with not being a man?
parts.note: read as a woman's statement: a will is what she handles, and she is not a man

explanation.surface: Someone anxiously wondering whether they will have to cope without being male.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as a future-tense auxiliary, but is the testament a woman appointed in it administers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman named in a testament to carry out its terms, the feminine form of executor.

clue.text: Reportedly snoops round for somewhere to fight

indicators.note: reportedly means what is spoken resembles another phrase

parts.note: snoops means pries, and a round shape is a ring

explanation.surface: Word has it that nosy parkers are circling a place for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing ring where bouts are fought for a purse is a place for fighting.

clue.text: Reticent criminal stopped by judge, say, abruptly

indicators.note: stopped by means the shuffled letters are plugged by the judge's letter
criminal means the letters of reticent are crooked, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped crook halted by a judge, who perhaps speaks curtly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped by' puts J into INTERECT, the rearrangement of RETICENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in with a remark is to speak suddenly, interrupting others.

clue.text: River — first of rivers not in sequence

indicators.note: not in means that letter is absent from the word for sequence

parts.note: an order is a sequence, an arrangement

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of rivers

explanation.surface: A river, the first of a list of rivers that are out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in sequence' looks like 'jumbled', but means the letter is not in the word for sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a central European river forming much of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Searching for blanket

definitions.meaning: a sweep is a thorough search of an area
a blanket statement is a comprehensive, all-embracing one

explanation.surface: Looking for a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep by police is a search, and a sweeping change is wholesale, broad, all-embracing.

clue.text: Search for degenerate

definitions.meaning: to comb through papers is to search them

explanation.surface: Looking for someone depraved.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through things thoroughly is to search them, and a debauched man is a libertine.

clue.text: Run into resistance in gamble to become a ballet dancer

parts.note: to ram something is to run into it

indicators.note: in tells us the resistance goes inside the gamble

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Taking a punt and hitting opposition on the way to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Rambert, Polish-born dancer, founded the company later called Rambert in London.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a ballet dancer and teacher before founding the company that bears her name.

clue.text: Wood taken after struggle fighting in Korea

indicators.note: after struggle means the letters have been wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: Timber seized after a fight during a war in Korea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting in Korea' suggests the Korean War, but means a Korean fighting art.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Korean martial art of kicks and punches, so it is fighting from Korea.

clue.text: Well-behaved soldier going about minor tasks for officer

definitions.text: soldier going about minor tasks for officer
definitions.meaning: an attendant soldier who carries out chores for an officer

explanation.surface: A disciplined soldier running errands for his officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat behaviour is orderly, and the military attendant serving an officer has the same name.

clue.text: For instance, notice detail

parts.note: as can mean for instance, such as
a sign is a notice posted up

explanation.surface: An example of a notice that pays attention to detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' looks like a noun, but is the military verb to allot someone a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail someone is to allocate them a duty, the same as appointing them to it.

clue.text: Upheaval as Merlot is replaced with Medoc at first

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a different order
at first means the opening letter of Medoc

explanation.surface: Turmoil when a Merlot is swapped for a Medoc at the start of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is replaced' looks like a swap of wine, but only the letters of AS MERLOT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool, figuratively a state of turbulent confusion, is a picture of upheaval.

clue.text: Expert in religious law off-duty cop may assume

definitions.meaning: a Muslim scholar who gives rulings on Islamic law
civilian clothes, worn by service people off duty

explanation.surface: A legal scholar whom an off-duty policeman might pretend to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' reads as suppose, but means put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim legal scholar has this title, and the same word means plain clothes worn off duty.

clue.text: Simple anagram clue in crossword, finally correct…

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A setter admits an easy anagram clue in the puzzle is finally right.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like it holds an anagram, but none is there.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, a synonym used of editing.

clue.text: …but on reflection the setter's devious

indicators.note: on reflection means that word is seen in a mirror, read backwards

parts.note: save, like but, can mean except
the setter speaks as I, so the setter's, the setter has, is I've

explanation.surface: Following on, the setter confesses that, thinking it over, the clue was devious.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's surface but not its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shifty who dodges direct answers is devious, sly or slippery.

clue.text: More suitable container for right kind of food

indicators.note: container for means the word for more suitable holds the letter for right

parts.note: fitter means more appropriate

explanation.surface: A better box for keeping the right sort of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Batter-coated fried fruit, vegetable or meat is a dish, a sort of food.

clue.text: United maybe dropping English or Scottish cap

indicators.note: dropping means that letter falls out

parts.note: Manchester United is a football team

explanation.surface: A club like United leaving out an English or a Scottish player's cap.
explanation.walkthrough: A cap in football is an international appearance, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: This woollen bonnet, short for tam-o'-shanter, is traditional Scottish headwear.

clue.text: Clear about accepting agreement that's symbolic

indicators.note: accepting means the turned word takes in the agreement
about means that word is turned round

parts.note: to clear a profit is to net it
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Plainly concerned with taking on an agreement that is only a gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to make as profit; 'about' turns it round and 'accepting' takes the agreement inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is symbolic, done for show rather than substance.

clue.text: Prune, sticky one I can't recall

parts.note: to prune a hedge is to thin it
gummy means sticky

explanation.surface: A sticky dried plum whose name escapes me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prune' looks like the fruit, but is the verb to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a placeholder word for an item whose name has been forgotten, like whatsit.
